careers.title: Software Developer
careers.shortDescription: Design and build applications, websites, and systems that people use every day.
careers.overview: Software developers turn requirements into working software. The day-to-day work mixes writing code, reviewing other people's code, debugging, and discussing what to build with teammates. Entry routes vary: many roles ask for a computer science or related degree, while others accept diplomas or a strong portfolio of projects.
responsibilities: Write, test, and maintain code for features and fixes
Break down requirements into small, reviewable tasks
Debug errors and improve performance
Review teammates' code and share feedback
Write documentation so others can use the work
educationPathways: Bachelor's degree in computer science, IT, or a related field (common route)
Diploma plus a strong project portfolio is accepted by some employers
Self-directed learning with published projects, where employers allow it
beginnerProjects: Build a to-do or notes app with add, edit, and delete
Create a personal portfolio website that works on phones
Consume a public API and display the results in a clean layout
skillsToLearn: How the web works: HTTP, APIs, and JSON
careers.educationNote: Employer requirements differ widely; check each job listing.

careers.title: Data Analyst
careers.shortDescription: Turn raw data into clear answers, dashboards, and recommendations for decisions.
careers.overview: Data analysts collect, clean, and interpret data so organisations can make evidence-based decisions. The role uses spreadsheets, SQL, and visualisation tools more than advanced mathematics, which makes it an approachable entry point into data careers. Degrees in statistics, economics, commerce, or computer science are common, but demonstrated skill through projects matters to many employers.
responsibilities: Collect and clean data from multiple sources
Build queries to extract and transform records
Create dashboards and charts that explain trends
Summarise findings for non-technical stakeholders
Track metrics and flag unusual changes
educationPathways: Bachelor's degree in statistics, economics, commerce, or computer science (common)
Diploma or certificate pathways with a portfolio of analyses
Career switches supported by practical, published case studies
beginnerProjects: Analyse a public dataset and publish a short written summary
Build a spreadsheet dashboard with charts for a topic you care about
Answer five real questions about a dataset using SQL
skillsToLearn: A plotting or BI tool of your choice
careers.educationNote: Tools and SQL skill are often assessed through practical tests.

careers.title: Machine Learning Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Build models that learn from data to power predictions and recommendations.
careers.overview: Machine learning engineers adapt statistical and software engineering methods so systems can learn patterns from data. The role sits between software development and applied research: strong programming plus solid mathematics are both important. Most advertised positions expect at least a bachelor's degree in a quantitative field, and many prefer a master's; some research teams require more.
responsibilities: Prepare and validate training data
Train, evaluate, and compare models
Package models so applications can use them
Monitor model behaviour after release
Document experiments and results honestly
educationPathways: Bachelor's in computer science, mathematics, statistics, or a related field
Master's degree is common for research-leaning roles
Coursework plus reproducible project work for entry-level positions
beginnerProjects: Train a text or image classifier on a public dataset
Recreate a simple classic model from scratch in code
Build an end-to-end demo: data, model, and a small web page
skillsToLearn: Evaluation metrics and avoiding data leakage
careers.educationNote: Degree expectations vary; research roles usually ask for higher qualifications.

careers.title: Cybersecurity Analyst
careers.shortDescription: Protect systems and data by finding weaknesses and responding to threats.
careers.overview: Cybersecurity analysts monitor systems, investigate suspicious activity, and harden infrastructure against attacks. The work blends technical investigation with clear reporting, since findings must be explained to teams that fix them. Entry commonly expects IT or computer science study, though certifications and demonstrated lab work are accepted in some organisations.
responsibilities: Monitor alerts and investigate security incidents
Run vulnerability scans and track remediation
Apply patches and review system configurations
Document incidents and recommend improvements
Educate colleagues about safe practices
educationPathways: Bachelor's in computer science, IT, or cybersecurity (common)
Diploma plus lab portfolio and industry certifications
Lateral entry from sysadmin or network roles for some employers
beginnerProjects: Set up a home lab and practise securing a small network
Complete beginner capture-the-flag challenges
Audit your own machine and write a short hardening checklist
careers.educationNote: Certifications are valued by some employers, not all; check individual listings.

careers.title: UI/UX Designer
careers.shortDescription: Shape how digital products look, feel, and flow for the people who use them.
careers.overview: UI/UX designers plan and visualise product interfaces: what a screen contains, how a user moves through it, and how it feels to use. The role combines research, wireframing, visual design, and close work with developers. Degrees in design or human-computer interaction help, but a well-explained portfolio is often the deciding factor.
responsibilities: Research user needs and pain points
Sketch wireframes and user flows
Build interactive prototypes
Create visual styles: colour, type, spacing
Test with users and revise designs
educationPathways: Bachelor's in design, fine arts, or human-computer interaction (common)
Diploma or certificate programmes in UX design
Portfolio-led entry for career switchers with transferable skills
beginnerProjects: Redesign a screen of an app you use daily and explain why
Interview three people about one problem and draft a solution
Build a clickable prototype of a small multi-screen flow
skillsToLearn: Presenting design rationale in writing and speech
careers.educationNote: Most design hiring reviews portfolios first; ask each studio or team about their process.

careers.title: Electronics Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Design, test, and improve the circuits and devices behind modern technology.
careers.overview: Electronics engineers work on circuit design, signal handling, and the devices that contain them, from sensors to consumer products. The role is hands-on with measurement instruments alongside simulation and documentation. A bachelor's degree in electronics or a closely related discipline is the usual entry route, with licensing rules differing by country.
responsibilities: Design and simulate circuits
Build prototypes and measure performance
Select components against cost and availability
Write test plans and interpret results
Document designs for production teams
educationPathways: Bachelor's in electronics and communication or electronics engineering (common)
Diploma in electronics technology for technician-level roles
Relevant project experience for support engineering roles
beginnerProjects: Build a sensor-reading circuit and log the values
Design a simple power supply on a breadboard
Simulate an amplifier circuit and compare with measurements
skillsToLearn: Embedded C or Python for test automation
careers.educationNote: Professional licensing rules vary by country and employer.

careers.title: Embedded Systems Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Write the software that runs inside devices, from appliances to vehicles.
careers.overview: Embedded engineers build software and firmware that runs on dedicated hardware with tight limits on memory and power. The work sits between electronics and software: reading datasheets, driving sensors, and debugging with instruments. Employers often look for electronics, electrical, or computer engineering degrees plus evidence of hands-on projects.
responsibilities: Write firmware for microcontrollers
Interface with sensors and communication buses
Optimise memory and power usage
Debug with logic analysers and oscilloscopes
Validate behaviour against requirements
educationPathways: Bachelor's in electronics, electrical, or computer engineering (common)
Diploma with strong practical project work
Portfolios of working devices for roles that accept them
beginnerProjects: Blink an LED, then add a button and serial output on a dev board
Read a temperature sensor and display readings
Build a small robot or controller that reacts to its environment
careers.educationNote: Project evidence is weighed heavily; requirements still differ per employer.

careers.title: Electrical Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Work with power systems, machines, and the electrical infrastructure around us.
careers.overview: Electrical engineers deal with power generation and distribution, machines, control systems, and electrical safety. Depending on the employer, work can range from field inspections to simulation and design office tasks. A bachelor's degree in electrical engineering is the standard entry route, and professional certification rules apply in many regions.
responsibilities: Design and review electrical layouts and panels
Perform load calculations and safety checks
Test equipment and record readings
Coordinate with construction or production teams
Maintain documentation and compliance records
educationPathways: Bachelor's in electrical engineering (common route)
Diploma in electrical technology for technician positions
Internships with utilities or contractors for practical entry
beginnerProjects: Map and measure the wiring of a simple model circuit
Build a small motor-speed control circuit
Study energy use of household devices and chart the results
skillsToLearn: Electrical safety standards used in your region
careers.educationNote: Licensing and safety regulations vary by country and employer.

careers.title: Mechanical Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Design and test the physical machines, parts, and systems people rely on.
careers.overview: Mechanical engineers apply mechanics, materials, and thermal science to design products and processes. The role moves between CAD modelling, calculation, prototyping, and testing on the shop floor. A bachelor's degree in mechanical or a related engineering discipline is the usual requirement for graduate positions.
responsibilities: Create and revise 3D models and drawings
Run basic stress, thermal, or motion calculations
Prototype parts and evaluate test results
Work with manufacturing teams on tolerances
Maintain design documentation
educationPathways: Bachelor's in mechanical or production engineering (common)
Diploma in mechanical technology for technician roles
Project and workshop experience supporting early applications
beginnerProjects: Model a simple part in CAD and 3D-print or sketch it
Measure the efficiency of a small mechanism you own
Build a basic machine (bridge, crane, or gearbox) and load-test it
careers.educationNote: Employer requirements vary; some roles prefer chartered status later on.

careers.title: Robotics Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Combine mechanics, electronics, and code to make machines that sense and act.
careers.overview: Robotics engineers integrate mechanical design, electronics, and software so machines can perceive their surroundings and perform tasks. The field is broad and interdisciplinary; entry roles commonly ask for a bachelor's in robotics, mechanical, electrical, or computer engineering, with strong evidence of integrated projects.
responsibilities: Integrate sensors and actuators with control code
Prototype and iterate on mechanical assemblies
Implement motion planning or simple control logic
Test robots against real-world conditions
Document systems so teammates can extend them
educationPathways: Bachelor's in robotics, mechanical, electrical, or computer engineering
Master's for specialised research positions
Competition teams and project portfolios strengthening applications
beginnerProjects: Build a line-following robot
Control a robotic arm with joint limits in software
Add distance sensing to avoid obstacles on a small rover
careers.educationNote: Projects and competition experience are often as important as grades.

careers.title: Civil Engineer
careers.shortDescription: Plan and supervise the buildings, roads, and infrastructure communities depend on.
careers.overview: Civil engineers design and coordinate infrastructure such as buildings, roads, drainage, and utilities, balancing safety, cost, and site conditions. The work includes calculations, drawings, site visits, and coordination with many parties. A bachelor's in civil engineering is the standard entry, with professional registration expected for signing off designs in most regions.
responsibilities: Prepare structural and site calculations
Read and produce drawings and schedules
Inspect sites and check work against drawings
Coordinate with architects, contractors, and clients
Keep records for quality and compliance
educationPathways: Bachelor's in civil engineering (common route)
Diploma in civil technology for site technician roles
Internships with construction or consultancy firms
beginnerProjects: Survey a small area and produce a scaled sketch
Design and load-test a model bridge
Measure quantities for a simple room and draft a bill of materials
careers.educationNote: Site work and regional registration rules vary; confirm locally.

careers.title: Research Scientist
careers.shortDescription: Ask new questions, design studies, and add evidence to a field of knowledge.
careers.overview: Research scientists plan studies, collect and interpret evidence, and communicate findings through papers and talks. The path usually runs through advanced degrees: most advertised research roles expect a master's at minimum and a PhD for independent positions. Persistence, careful methodology, and writing matter as much as raw technical skill.
responsibilities: Review existing literature and identify gaps
Design experiments or studies with clear methods
Analyse results and test their reliability
Write papers and grant proposals
Present findings to colleagues and conferences
educationPathways: Bachelor's then Master's in a science or engineering discipline
PhD for independent research positions (common requirement)
Research assistant roles as an intermediate step
beginnerProjects: Reproduce a small published result and document the process
Run a controlled experiment with a clear hypothesis
Write a literature review on a topic you care about
careers.educationNote: Qualification requirements are strict in many institutions — verify per programme.

careers.title: Business Analyst
careers.shortDescription: Translate business problems into clear requirements and measurable improvements.
careers.overview: Business analysts sit between stakeholders and delivery teams: they gather needs, map processes, and define what a solution must achieve. The role leans on communication and structured thinking more than programming. Degrees in business, commerce, IT, or engineering are common backgrounds; analytical evidence through projects helps a great deal.
responsibilities: Interview stakeholders and capture requirements
Map current processes and find bottlenecks
Define acceptance criteria for solutions
Build reports that track outcomes
Facilitate workshops and keep records
educationPathways: Bachelor's in business, commerce, economics, or IT (common)
MBA or business analysis certifications for progression
Internal transfers from operations or support roles
beginnerProjects: Write requirements for an app idea, including edge cases
Analyse a small business's process and propose three improvements
Build a dashboard that answers five stakeholder questions
careers.educationNote: Certifications valued differ by employer; check individual postings.

careers.title: Financial Analyst
careers.shortDescription: Study numbers, markets, and reports to guide money-related decisions.
careers.overview: Financial analysts review financial statements, build models, and summarise performance for teams that allocate money. Accuracy and clear explanation are essential. Employers commonly ask for degrees in finance, economics, commerce, or accounting; some also expect progress toward professional finance certifications.
responsibilities: Build and maintain financial models
Review budgets, forecasts, and actual results
Research industries and companies
Prepare summaries and presentations
Check data quality before reporting
educationPathways: Bachelor's in finance, economics, commerce, or accounting (common)
Professional certifications valued by some employers
Analyst internships as an entry point
beginnerProjects: Build a budget and track it for three months
Analyse a public company's annual report and write a one-page note
Compare two options (buy vs rent, plan A vs plan B) with a simple model
skillsToLearn: SQL or Python for data handling
careers.educationNote: Certification expectations differ by employer and country.

careers.title: Digital Marketing Specialist
careers.shortDescription: Plan and measure online campaigns that help people discover products and ideas.
careers.overview: Digital marketing specialists work across content, search, social, and paid campaigns, then read the results to decide what to improve. The role suits people who enjoy a mix of writing, design, and analysis. Formal degrees vary widely; demonstrable campaign work and platform knowledge often carry more weight than a specific major.
responsibilities: Plan campaign messaging and schedules
Set up tracking and read analytics reports
Write or brief short-form content
Test variations and compare results
Report what worked and what to change
educationPathways: Bachelor's in marketing, commerce, media, or communications (common but not universal)
Certificate courses plus a personal project portfolio
Freelance or club campaign experience for entry
beginnerProjects: Run a small campaign for a college club and report results
Write ten SEO-focused articles for a topic you know well
Design a content calendar and measure engagement for a month
careers.educationNote: Platform certifications are optional and change often; verify current offers.

careers.title: Technical Writer
careers.shortDescription: Explain complex products and technology in docs people can actually follow.
careers.overview: Technical writers turn complicated subject matter into clear documentation: guides, references, release notes, and tutorials. The role rewards strong writing paired with enough technical understanding to ask the right questions. English, communications, or technical backgrounds all appear in the field; writing samples decide most hiring.
responsibilities: Interview subject-matter experts
Draft and structure documentation
Keep content accurate as products change
Edit for clarity, consistency, and tone
Maintain doc sites and style guidelines
educationPathways: Bachelor's in English, communications, or a technical discipline (both appear)
Documentation portfolios for career switchers
Open-source contributions as evidence of practice
beginnerProjects: Write setup docs for a project of your own, then hand them to a friend
Improve the documentation of an open-source tool
Create a five-step tutorial with screenshots for a common task
careers.educationNote: Writing samples usually matter more than a specific degree; check per employer.

careers.title: STEM Educator
careers.shortDescription: Help students understand science, technology, engineering, and maths through teaching.
careers.overview: STEM educators design lessons, demonstrate concepts, and support students until ideas click. The work is people-centred: patience, clarity, and subject knowledge all matter. School-level teaching typically requires a teaching qualification or degree in the subject, while tutoring, corporate training, and content creation have different entry requirements — always verify locally.
responsibilities: Plan lessons and learning activities
Explain concepts with examples and demos
Assess student understanding and adapt
Give constructive feedback
Keep records and communicate with families or managers
educationPathways: Bachelor's in the subject plus a teaching qualification (common for schools)
Tutoring and online teaching with demonstrated subject skill
Corporate training roles valuing industry experience
beginnerProjects: Teach a short class or workshop to younger students
Build a set of flashcards or problems with worked solutions
Record a five-minute explanation of a concept you find tricky
skillsToLearn: Giving feedback that students can act on
careers.educationNote: Teaching requirements differ by country, institution, and level taught.
